baseline_models.focus_anchor: The paired construction "they said ... and the Messiah said" sets the identity claim against the Messiah's own command to worship God, his Lord and theirs.
baseline_models.mechanism: The two قول occurrences stage rival positions rather than one continuous report. The first assigns an identity to the Messiah; the second gives his own relational grammar, in which worship runs toward God and both speaker and audience stand under shared lordship. The first claim is therefore exposed as an attribution that displaces the subject's own testimony.

activation_trace.role: قول as belief or position makes the two clauses competing commitments, with the Messiah's own commitment testing the claim made about him.
The branch of attributing what was not said makes the first statement function as an imposed account that the second statement visibly contradicts.
Submissive worship supplies the relation the Messiah commands and directs it away from himself toward God.
Lordship, ownership, and rule are shared over the speaker and audience, placing both on one governed level.

changed_reading.before: The ayah merely rejects a doctrinal identification.
changed_reading.after: The ayah conducts a counter-testimony: an attributed identity is judged by the Messiah's own speech, whose worship and shared-lord syntax places him with his audience under God.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The same بنى root marks the Messiah as Mary's son and the audience as the sons of Israel, immediately before "my Lord and your Lord."
baseline_models.mechanism: Both filiation phrases locate persons in chains of descent or origin. Their parallel placement, followed by shared lordship, levels the named Messiah and the addressed community as derivative members under one ruler; filiation cannot by itself cross into the rank of the worshiped.

activation_trace.role: Filiation and attribution to an origin join "son of Mary" and "sons of Israel" as parallel derivative placements.
The repeated possessives distribute one sovereign lordship over both the Messiah and those he addresses.
The worshiped-object branch keeps divinity tied to the repeatedly named God while the Messiah occupies the speaking and worship-commanding position.

changed_reading.before: The title "son of Mary" is only biographical identification.
changed_reading.after: Its repetition against "sons of Israel" becomes an anti-elevation device: both genealogical expressions remain below the shared lordship named by the Messiah.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The sequence runs from كفر to God's barring of الجنة.
baseline_models.mechanism: The focus places two kinds of covering in tension. كفر covers or occludes the truth, while جنة is a protected, tree-covered enclosure. The first covering triggers حرمان, so a chosen concealment blocks access to a sheltering concealment.

activation_trace.role: Covering the truth names the initiating epistemic act that hides the God-Messiah distinction.
The tree-covered garden supplies the protected enclosure from which the truth-covering act excludes its agent.
Deprivation and loss of the sought good turn the two coverings into a gate consequence rather than a loose word association.

changed_reading.before: Disbelief and loss of the garden are simply offense and punishment.
changed_reading.after: They form a covering paradox: obscuring the relational truth prevents entry into the protective enclosure, so the punishment mirrors the mechanism of the offense.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Whoever يشرك is barred from the garden, has fire as مأوى, and has no أنصار.
baseline_models.mechanism: Partnership changes exclusive worship into a divided stake. The resulting exclusion is also a forced belonging: مأوى makes the agent join a gathering-place, but that place is fire rather than garden. ظلم names the misplacement, while the absence of helpers denies that social backing can repair the displaced relation.

activation_trace.role: Participation or shared stake supplies the relational mechanics of dividing what the worship command treats as exclusive.
Joining a side that gathers and houses turns punishment into an attachment or belonging, not only an external blow.
Kindled fire supplies the destination to which the false attachment now gathers.
Putting a thing outside its proper place makes the identity claim a relational misplacement with spatial consequences.
Aid that would make one prevail is explicitly absent, so communal endorsement cannot reverse the forced refuge.

changed_reading.before: Shirk is an abstract doctrinal error followed by unrelated penalties.
changed_reading.after: Shirk is a misplaced share that reorganizes belonging: exclusion from one enclosure becomes attachment to another, beyond the repair of social allies.

context_deltas.mechanism: At 5:61 people enter with kufr and leave with it, while God knows what they conceal. Entry and exit frame the cover as a persistent interior cargo. This strengthens the focus claim from an isolated bad sentence into the audible surface of a state carried through an encounter.

activation_trace.role: Truth-covering anchors the context's carried condition back in the focus verdict.
An inwardly embedded corruption gives the entering kufr an interior location rather than treating it as a momentary utterance.
The same truth-cover is explicitly carried into the encounter.
Movement back outside without losing the state supplies persistence across the encounter's boundary.
Concealment links the carried interior condition to an outwardly incomplete presentation.

structural_cues: 5:61 encloses kufr between دخلوا and خرجوا به, then closes with يكتمون.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies inward entry, outward exit, and concealment; I infer that the unchanged cargo is an interior orientation later voiced in 5:72. A live alternative is that 5:61 describes conduct at a particular encounter without defining every later utterance.

changed_reading.before: The condemned identity claim is a discrete verbal mistake.
changed_reading.after: It can be heard as the exposed form of a concealed orientation that enters and exits encounters intact.

context_deltas.mechanism: At 5:64 a statement about God casts the divine hand as bound, and the counterstatement renders the hands outspread. That claim-counterclaim supplies a material grammar for 5:72: saying that God is the embodied, genealogically located Messiah can be heard as verbally constricting divine agency into a bounded predicate.

activation_trace.role: The focus claim and counter-speech are held positions whose effects can be compared with the nearby claim-counterclaim.
A statement attributed about God is corrected by a counterstatement, supplying the contextual pattern of imposed speech.
The hand as authority makes binding and extension changes in represented divine agency, not merely limb posture.
A collar or binding that immobilizes an organ supplies the constriction pole of the speech mechanism.
Extension and release of the hand supplies the corrective expansion of agency.

structural_cues: 5:64 and 5:72 both pair a claim about God with corrective speech in the same extended discourse.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies claim, bodily binding, authority, and counter-expansion; I transfer constriction as an analogy to the identity equation in 5:72. The materially live alternative is that the two claims are separate errors with no shared constriction mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The equation of God and Messiah is false only at the level of classification.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the equation also performs a verbal binding: it compresses unbounded divine authority into an embodied and genealogically bounded predicate.

context_deltas.mechanism: At 5:65 belief and self-protection lead God to perform ك ف ر upon misdeeds and then cause entry into gardens. The same root therefore reverses by agent and object: humans cover truth and lose the garden; God covers faults and admits people into gardens. The focus is not a one-note cover lexeme but a directional economy of what is covered and by whom.

activation_trace.role: Human covering hides the truth and initiates the focus ayah's exclusion.
Heart-settling assent supplies the changed human orientation that precedes the reversal.
Placing oneself in protection supplies the guarded posture paired with belief.
Divine covering erases the effect of faults, reversing both agent and protected object of the focus root.
Caused entry supplies the opened gate that directly reverses the focus barring.
The covered gardens are now the destination reached after faults, rather than truth, are covered.

structural_cues: The conditional sequence in 5:65 is belief and guarding, then divine covering, then caused entry; 5:72 is shirk, then barring, then the opposed refuge.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies one root with opposite agents and an explicit entry sequence; I infer a directional reversal based on what the covering protects or obscures. A live alternative is to keep expiation and concealment lexically separate despite their shared packet branch family.

changed_reading.before: كفر has only the negative sense of disbelief that earns exclusion.
changed_reading.after: The context makes covering reversible: covering truth closes the garden, while God's covering of faults opens it, so agency and object determine the root's trajectory.

context_deltas.mechanism: The repeated opening at 5:73 moves from the focus identity equation to a counted relation, "third of three," and immediately counters it with one deity. This sharpens focus شرك as a structural operation: whether by equation or enumeration, speech redistributes singular divinity into a composite relation.

activation_trace.role: Shared stake supplies the focus mechanism that the following count makes structurally visible.
The repeated speech-position frame marks the counted proposition as a parallel commitment to the focus equation.
A third that completes a three-member whole materializes the partitioned relational structure.
Divine oneness without partner supplies the explicit counter-structure.

structural_cues: 5:73 repeats 5:72's لقد كفر الذين قالوا opening and places the counted claim directly against إلا إله واحد.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies parallel openings, equation, count, and singular counterclaim; I infer that 5:72 and 5:73 expose related ways of restructuring divinity. They may alternatively target distinct propositions whose only shared feature is rejection.

changed_reading.before: The focus identity claim and the following numerical claim are separate errors.
changed_reading.after: They become parallel partitioning operations: one equates God with a located person, the other counts a divine member, and both violate the unshared relation named by one deity.

context_deltas.mechanism: Immediately after the repeated threat, 5:74 asks for return and seeking cover, then names God as covering and merciful. This revises the focus barring from a closed metaphysical identity into the consequence of a maintained relation: return can change what is covered and reopen the trajectory.

activation_trace.role: Deprivation anchors the apparently closed consequence that the following invitation requalifies.
Calling another to return supplies an offered transition out of the condemned relation.
Covering a fault while shielding its agent from its effect supplies the mechanism by which the trajectory can change.
Merciful tenderness keeps the offered return from being a merely formal possibility.

structural_cues: 5:74's rhetorical invitation follows the threat of 5:73 without an intervening topic change.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies immediate return, requested covering, and mercy; I infer that the barring applies while shirk is maintained, not as an irreversible sentence before death. An alternative is that the attributes are general and the passage leaves the exact legal scope of reversal unstated.

changed_reading.before: Once named by the focus verdict, the person is permanently barred.
changed_reading.after: The verdict names a live trajectory of maintained shirk; the next ayah keeps a return route open through repentance, fault-covering, and mercy.

context_deltas.mechanism: At 5:75 the Messiah is restricted to a messenger in a temporal succession and is paired with his mother as two eaters of food. At 5:76 worship is tested by ownership of harm and benefit. Succession, nourishment, and limited disposal make the focus filiation and shared-lord syntax materially causal: a dependent recipient cannot occupy the source-level role to which worship is directed.

activation_trace.role: Genealogical derivation anchors the later tests back in the focus title and addressed lineage.
Messenger and message place the Messiah in a transmitting office rather than at the source of worship.
The passing of earlier messengers locates his office in a temporal succession.
Taking nourishment supplies embodied reception and recurring dependence.
Food as the object tasted makes the dependency concrete rather than merely titular.
Possession and power of disposal provide the explicit agency test for an object of worship.
Harm as loss supplies one outcome the proposed object does not control.
Benefit supplies the opposed outcome likewise outside the proposed object's disposal.

structural_cues: 5:75 uses nominal restriction for the Messiah, then a dual verb for him and his mother eating; 5:76 immediately asks whether what is below God owns harm or benefit.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies office, succession, nourishment, and lack-of-ownership testing; I infer that dependence disqualifies source-level lordship and explains the focus command. A live alternative is that eating establishes humanity while the agency question targets a broader class of worshiped objects.

changed_reading.before: The focus corrects a title by asserting monotheism.
changed_reading.after: The context turns the correction into a dependency test: a genealogically derived messenger who receives food and does not own outcomes stands with recipients under the Lord, not as their worshiped source.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus says wrongdoers have no helpers; 5:79 says people did not restrain one another from reprehensible action. Read together, help is not merely rescue after judgment. Its missing social form is corrective interruption before wrongdoing hardens; allies who never restrain cease to function as helpers.

activation_trace.role: Aid and making another prevail anchor the helper function that the later non-restraint fails to perform.
Withholding a right links wrongdoing to the social refusal to supply corrective aid.
Restraint from an act supplies the preventive form that genuine assistance could have taken.
The reprehensible act is something to be repelled, defining the target of corrective help.
Enacted work keeps the failure at the level of repeated social practice, not opinion alone.

structural_cues: The plural reciprocal يتناهون in 5:79 describes an absent within-group practice, while 5:72 closes with the plural absence of أنصار.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies absent rescue and absent mutual restraint; I infer that corrective restraint is an upstream form of help. The alternative is that 5:79 diagnoses communal misconduct without specifying what 5:72's final helpers would mean.

changed_reading.before: No helpers means only that nobody can rescue wrongdoers at the end.
changed_reading.after: It also exposes a prior social failure: companions who do not interrupt misplacement are not functioning as helpers even before final rescue becomes impossible.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later sequence describes people who say "we are Christians" as near in affection and not self-exalting, then moves through hearing, recognition, and a confession of belief, and finally rewards them with gardens because of what they said. This sharply differentiates the focus verdict: the operative issue is not the social label alone but what speech does with recognized truth and with the Messiah's own testimony.

activation_trace.role: Speech as held position anchors the focus condemnation to the content and relation enacted by a claim.
Nearness rather than distance supplies the changed social orientation of the later self-designated Christians.
Affection supplies the relational quality accompanying that nearness.
The statement "we are Christians" identifies a group whose subsequent speech trajectory differs from the focus proposition.
Negated self-greatness removes the elevation posture that would resist recognized truth.
Hearing as understanding and compliance starts the receptive sequence.
Recognition by sign differentiates receptive identification from an imposed identity statement.
Their spoken commitment follows hearing and recognition, reversing the focus order in which a claim suppresses counter-testimony.
Heart-settling assent names the commitment voiced after recognition.
A deed's returning recompense makes the speech sequence causally consequential.
Reward "because of what they said" makes proposition and enacted commitment, not label alone, the explicit hinge.
Admission to covered gardens directly reverses the focus exclusion for a different speech-response trajectory.

structural_cues: 5:72 and 5:82 both classify people through الذين قالوا, while 5:83 supplies hearing-recognition-saying and 5:85 explicitly rewards بما قالوا.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated saying formulas, Christian self-designation, receptive sequence, and reward; I infer that the focus verdict discriminates propositions and responses rather than fixing a blanket fate by label. A live alternative is that the later sequence concerns only a distinct subgroup and does not state a universal criterion.

changed_reading.before: The focus ayah reads as an undifferentiated verdict on everyone carrying a Christian designation.
changed_reading.after: Within the packet, it targets a specific truth-covering proposition: other self-designated Christians hear, recognize, speak belief, and receive the very gardens denied in the focus trajectory.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the focus fire is a terminal refuge while 5:64 names a fire of war. It remains anchored through the same packet fire root and the focus مأوى sequence, but it is an analogical social echo, not a replacement for punitive fire; downstream prose should say the focus fire may also evoke a conflict-producing trajectory.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus assigns fire as the shelter reached after a claim that displaces exclusive worship.

activation_trace.role: Joining a gathering side makes fire a chosen or forced relational destination.
The kindled fire anchors the contextual war-fire analogy in the focus noun.
Deliberate ignition supplies an upstream human action that generates the nearby fire.
The same fire branch materializes the hostile social state in the nearby discourse.
War and enmity specify the social domain of that contextual ignition.
God's cooling of the flame supplies a counter-action to recurrent human ignition.

changed_reading.before: The fire is only a remote penalty with no mechanism in the surrounding social field.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, it also echoes the recurrent fires of hostility generated by constrictive claims and alliances, even as God extinguishes their historical outbreaks.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This cross-domain material sequence is surprising because tears and rivers do not lexically interpret the focus fire. It remains validly anchored in the focus opposition between fire and garden and in the packet's later garden outcome; render it as an imagistic trajectory of reception, not as a doctrinal equivalence.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus moves from truth-covering speech to exclusion from the garden and attachment to fire.

activation_trace.role: Fire supplies the dry, consuming destination opposed by the later flow sequence.
The denied garden anchors the destination later reached through receptive speech.
Easy overflow turns recognition into bodily movement rather than a sealed interior claim.
The tear and its channel give the first flow a visible human medium.
Unimpeded running extends bodily overflow into the rewarded landscape.
A river cutting the earth with flowing water completes the counter-material destination inside the garden.

changed_reading.before: The focus offers only a static binary of garden versus fire.
changed_reading.after: As an imagistic outlier, the packet gives two trajectories: imposed speech seals into fire, while hearing and recognition overflow through tears into the rivers of the reopened garden.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is form-distant because it uses the packet's non-dominant ق ل ل mapping for the focus قول root. It is still anchored by that explicit split inventory and by the paired قول construction, but it should be rendered only as a phonetic-branch activation suggesting instability, never as the lexical gloss of قالوا.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus juxtaposes two قول clauses whose relational claims cannot remain stable together.

activation_trace.role: Oscillation and lack of fixedness make the paired sayings register as an unstable claim displaced by the Messiah's counter-speech.
The repeated saying frame and shift into numerical formulation extend the formal sense of doctrinal movement rather than settled singularity.

changed_reading.before: The two reported sayings are semantically opposed but formally inert.
changed_reading.after: As a contained sound-branch activation, their juxtaposition also enacts instability: the imposed identity cannot settle beside the Messiah's own worship relation and shifts again into counted divinity.

strongest_changes: The same ك ف ر root reverses from human covering of truth and garden exclusion in 5:72 to divine covering of faults and garden admission in 5:65.
The immediate invitation to return, seek covering, and encounter mercy makes the exclusion a maintained trajectory rather than an irreversibly fixed identity.
Messenger succession, eating, and the ownership test turn the Messiah's filiation and shared-lord syntax into a concrete dependency argument.
The 5:82-85 hearing-recognition-saying sequence distinguishes Christian responses by proposition and reception, culminating in gardens because of what they said.
summary.what_was_special: The packet repeatedly makes speech causal: imposed claims constrict, cover, and partition, while heard and recognized truth becomes a different saying whose consequence is admission. The most diagnostic activation was not a broad theme but the reversal of who covers what.
remaining_uncertainties: The transfer from bound and outspread hands in 5:64 to the identity equation as verbal constriction is analogical and remains exploratory.
The war-fire and tears-to-rivers readings are material echoes, not semantic replacements for the focus destinations.
The packet opens repentance after the threat but does not spell out every temporal or legal boundary of that reopening.
The later receptive Christians may be a delimited subgroup; the packet supports differentiation but not a universal sociological rule.
